nodes.note: Root. Committed run. Nominal n=160 is 40 distinct sign draws — see phase0.md D2 (score_completion reseeds the global RNG, so trials 2-8 repeat trial 2's hidden set). The gate quantities reproduce: 0.0000, 0 recovered, NO SIGNAL. chance 0.0208 belongs to that entangled sequence; over 8 independent draws it is 0.0273 (guard 8 asserts the gate quantities, not chance).

Six defects repaired (incl. the 1.28x anchor-word leak, which was the only spurious positive). Oracle re-run unchanged at 0.00x: a zero multiplied by anything is zero, but this one was measured by repaired machinery. A seventh defect found 2026-09-30 is recorded in phase0.md.

Independently written instrument: one sign at a time, context-profile cosine against candidate-bearing anchors plus series/vowel votes, no shared code with the shipped scorer. Lands exactly on the majority-class baseline — the shipped code was not uniquely bad.
Multi-pass coordinate ascent from several initialisations on the same objective: 0/60. Search is not the limiting factor — the objective has no resolution to optimise.

nodes.source: pipeline/aggregator_bakeoff.py (this run, n=500: 25 trials x 20 hidden)
nodes.note: Eight aggregators incl. the shipped sum, kober-only, Borda rank-normalisation and the two-stage kober-then-entropy variant. Unique-argmax rate 0.0% for all eight. The docstring's 67/47/59/100% top-1 figures are pre-repair and do not reproduce.

Permutation control for op2b, same draws. Every channel's in_argmax is BELOW its null (0.25-0.52x): the 27-36% figures were argmax sets covering ~59% of the candidate list, not orientation. This is the measurement that retires PLAN §6.4's tie-collapse hypothesis and with it op5 (PLAN §8.4).

Kober's own recorded relation, four directions, all at or below chance. primary_metric is the consonant direction because that is the one Kober's method needs; the verdict is not taken from the best of the four (§8.3).

Per-sign use of the same relation, not the pairwise table: link-vote series 22.9% vs a 22.5% majority baseline, so 1.02x. The context-profile series rate 35.7% is the strongest number recorded anywhere in this project, and its null is NOT measured on the same draw set (the script's own uniform 1.3% is the wrong null for a class metric) — so it is carried as an unvalidated sub-metric, not as this node's primary. If a channel is ever worth a real node, it is this one, with a same-draw null.

Definition A (shared slot). Ventris's actual method. Slot-alternating partners share a series at roughly HALF the majority baseline — anti-predictive. The eliminative vowel step's 9/9 is n=9 (protocol §7: a plausible number outrunning its control) and its control reaches 73.8% by accident. primary_metric is the series ratio, the paper's conclusion 1.

Definition B, the strictest available (word types differing in exactly one position). Signal and permutation control converge: 78.6% vs 80.0%, and the eliminative step fires less often than its own control (19.4% vs 18.5% -> 1.05x). Built because definition A failed its control.
Cypro-Minoan is a direct daughter script of Linear A; ~30 LA values free if it breaks. Currently a synthetic placeholder. The only move that can raise the ceiling.
The continuous transliteration of the Knossos scepter (KN Zg 57/58), 119 signs, ritual — the first genuinely new long text since the corpus correction, and the correct re-test case for op4b.
Evidence class #1 in §7: semantic anchors. The failure of distributional methods says nothing about a bilingual of adequate length.

The seventh repair, and the first one that MOVES the number: 0/160 -> 1/160, lift 0.00x -> 0.23x. Cause: score_completion reseeded the global RNG, so the committed '8 trials' were 2 distinct hidden sets (trial 1 alone, then the same set seven times). With 8 genuinely independent draws the oracle now reports 0.0063 vs chance 0.0273 (chance 0.0208 -> 0.0273 for the same reason) and the verdict is unchanged: NO SIGNAL, 0.23x, still below chance. The single hit is attributable, and it is not signal: AB 01, hidden in 1 of 8 trials and recovered there, via a TIE resolved by candidate-list order - the unique-argmax rate over these same draws is 0.0%. AB 01 is the sign with the most corpus occurrences (640) and one of the two signs the original anchor-word leak produced (1.28x, repaired in op1a). Evaluated tie-strictly (rsi_evaluate), the shipped config still returns 0 recovered. The repair is behaviour-neutral for scoring: all 3,311 (sign, candidate) component tuples are bit-identical before and after.

The retrace's open item 1 (a per-sign channel that models the sign itself), measured against a same-draw permutation control: 25 trials x 20 hidden = 500 independent draws. The null gets its own RNG stream so the control cannot perturb the draw sequence it controls.
PRIMARY is series-vs-majority at 1.21x - chosen over the better class number, per PLAN §7.1's rule that a node must not be scored on the best of its metrics. INCONCLUSIVE (0.5-1.5) and below the pre-registered 1.5x.
The (series,vowel) class axis is stronger: 9.6% exact class pick vs a 2.4% majority baseline (4.00x) and a 2.4% permutation null (3.93x) - the strongest controlled result in this project. Recorded as a metric and claimed as nothing more: the 1.5x gate was pre-registered for exact-value lift over uniform chance, and a class is not a value.
Exact value is 0.0% BY CONSTRUCTION: in a syllabary one value belongs to one sign, so hiding the sign removes its value from the anchor set and the anchor support of the only right candidate is empty. No hide-N-recover instrument can measure a value-level per-sign channel; it can measure class information only. That is a structural reason for METHOD_CLOSURE_PAPER.md §4.1, not an empirical one.
Two corrections made before committing this node, both recorded because they are the project's own failure modes: (1) at 73 draws the series rate read 1.52x, above the gate, against a null stable at 14.7% - small-sample noise, which is why n=500 is recorded here; (2) the channel was first called per hidden sign instead of per trial, overstating n by 20x (8820 -> 500) with rates unaffected.

Ceiling for op2d, and the reason its class signal is not convertible. The true (series,vowel) class is handed over FOR FREE - this is an oracle restriction, not the channel's 9.6% prediction - so it is generous to the channel in the only direction that matters.
Result: within a 2.32-candidate class, the shipped scorer picks the right member 8.5% of the time against a 47.4% chance rate = 0.18x = NO SIGNAL. Tie-lenient (truth in the argmax set) 35.2% = 0.74x. The scorer is WORSE THAN RANDOM among class peers: it actively prefers the less typical member, which is what a frequency/typicality objective does.
Consequence: no improvement to the class channel - not even a perfect one - can yield values with this scorer. End-to-end estimate 0.096 x 0.085 = 0.81% absolute against a 2.5% uniform chance rate (0.33x). Ceiling, not sample size, is the binding constraint.
Also measured: the true class is only present in the candidate list on 44.4% of draws, and when present the truth always survives within it - the restriction is sound, the candidate generation is what removes the answer.
Pre-registered before the run in the script's docstring: within-class accuracy at or below 1/|class|. It held (0.18x). Recording it as a prediction that was written down first, and confirmed, is the only thing that distinguishes this from a number found and then explained.

Corrects the DENOMINATOR for op2b/op2c, and corrects one of this project's own nulls. Two separate defects in how the earlier numbers were read:
1. Membership. The true value is a candidate on only 54.2% of draws here, and on 36.2% of oracle_diagnose part B's 80 draws - so on ~half of all draws NO aggregator can be right, and averaging them in dilutes every rate by ~2x.
2. The null had 100% membership. phase0_null_control.py replaced the truth with a candidate DRAWN FROM the candidate list, so its 'truth' was always present while the real truth was present ~40-54% of the time. The null was solving an easier problem, and its 0.25-0.52x win was that asymmetry as much as flatness. This node recomputes everything conditional on the truth being in the list, with a within-subset null (a random OTHER candidate from the same list).
With the corrected denominator the conclusion SURVIVES, and for the right reasons:
  * unique argmax is 0.0% for all nine channels, even on identifiable draws. The closure paper's §4.1 claim holds.
  * in_argmax equals its mechanical tie rate (morph 66.1% vs 66.8% null; entropy 50.2 vs 50.9; prefix 52.8 vs 53.9). The high in_argmax figures were argmax-set SIZE, not orientation - and the argmax sets are huge (morph's covers two thirds of the candidate list).
  * mean rank is at the null for every channel (0.406-0.507 vs 0.488-0.503): no channel orders the truth above a random candidate even in the favourable subset.
  * TWO-STAGE (op5) in the subset: in_argmax 8.5% vs 7.0% null. PLAN §6.4's tie-collapse hypothesis is dead under the corrected denominator too.
It also resolves the apparent contradiction PLAN §6.4 was built on. aggregator_bakeoff.py's docstring says the components rank truth top-1 at 67/47/59/100% - measured here as in_argmax (ties allowed), morph 67~66, entropy 47~50 and prefix 59~53 DO reproduce; they are argmax-set size, not identification. KOBER's 100% is the one that does not reproduce: 8.9% here, 4.8% averaged over all draws. oracle_diagnose part C prints the same ties-allowed quantity under the label 'top-1', which is where the misreading starts; its 69/59/55 for morph/entropy/prefix match this node's in_argmax figures.
Practical consequence: candidate generation, not aggregation, is the first fixable defect - ~46% of draws are void before any scoring happens. The aggregation defect is second (the shipped sum is BELOW its own components: 5.2% vs 66.1% in_argmax). Neither is fixable by a better optimiser, which is what the closure paper §8 says.
